title: Expense policy for real estate and construction companies
summary: Add practical clauses for site purchases, per diems, tools, fuel, project coding, and UAE VAT evidence to your property or construction expense policy.
body_markdown:
A site engineer discovers a missing fitting at 4 pm. The supplier is nearby, but the usual buyer has gone home. A generic expense policy template may cover office supplies, travel, and client meals while giving the engineer no workable way to keep the job moving.


Property and construction teams also buy consumables, work away from base, fuel vehicles across sites, and need to charge costs to the right project. The policy has to answer four questions at the point of purchase: who can buy, how much, who approves, and what evidence to collect.


This article supplies those extra clauses. For the general structure, see[how to write a spending policy](https://www.alaan.com/blog/expense-policy-with-template) . Teams managing several properties can also see Alaan’s[spend management for real estate groups](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) . A rule nobody can follow on site soon teaches people to work around finance.


## Five clauses to add to your expense policy template


These expense policy examples are wording to adapt. Replace every bracketed amount, deadline, and role with an approved decision for your business.


### Urgent site purchases


Allow essential materials that cannot wait for the usual order route. Set both a purchase cap and a weekly site cap; above either, require a call to the project manager before paying. Require the item, reason, project code, supplier tax invoice, and same-day record. The site manager confirms the need; finance checks the evidence.


Clause to copy: “Site staff may buy essential materials up to AED \[amount\] per purchase and AED \[amount\] per site per week when waiting for a purchase order would delay approved work. Call \[role\] before exceeding either cap. Submit the reason, project code, and supplier tax invoice by \[time\]. Do not split an order to avoid approval.”


### Per diems and accommodation away from base


Define when an assignment qualifies, who books accommodation, and whether meals use an allowance or actual receipts. Set the amounts from recent costs in the assignment location. Record the site, dates, and hotel invoice; the project manager approves the assignment and any extra nights. Deduct meals already included in the booking.


Clause to copy: “For an approved assignment more than \[distance or travel time\] from the usual base, \[role\] may authorise accommodation up to AED \[amount\] per night and meals up to AED \[amount\] per day. Record the assignment and dates. Meals included with accommodation cannot be claimed again.”


### Tools, consumables, and subcontractor spend


Let an authorised site role buy low-value consumables within a project cap. Require prior approval and a register entry for reusable tools. If a subcontractor buys for you, say in its contract whether the purchase is included in its fee or reimbursable; the project manager approves any extra before purchase. Keep the supplier invoice and proof the goods reached the site.


Clause to copy: “Consumables up to AED \[amount\] may be bought by \[role\] for an approved project. Reusable tools require \[role\] approval and a register entry. Subcontractor purchases are reimbursable only if the contract allows them or \[role\] approves them in writing.”


### Vehicle, fuel, and mileage spend


Use a vehicle ID for fleet fuel and require the date, driver, site or route, litres, and receipt. For private vehicles, set a mileage rate and require a journey log. The fleet manager reviews unusual top-ups; finance checks for duplicate mileage and fuel claims. Use actual fleet patterns to set limits. See[mileage and fuel reimbursement](https://www.alaan.com/blog/employee-mileage-fuel-reimbursement-policies) for the wider rule.


Clause to copy: “Fuel claims must show the vehicle ID, driver, date, work route or site, and receipt. Approved private-vehicle trips use AED \[amount\] per kilometre and a journey log. Staff cannot claim both fuel and mileage for the same trip.”


### Property and project coding


Require a property or project code for every site purchase, plus a unit or work order when relevant. The site manager confirms which job benefited. Finance approves corrections and uses a documented method for costs shared between projects. No spend threshold is needed: even a small item can land in the wrong project budget.


Clause to copy: “Every site expense must include a property or project code and, where relevant, a work order or unit reference. Shared costs use \[allocation method\]. \[Role\] confirms the receiving project; finance approves later coding changes.”


## Set limits people can follow


Build an approval table by role, purchase type, and site. It should show what staff may buy directly, the amount that requires a call first, and who answers when the usual manager is unavailable. Use recent transactions, accommodation prices, and the cost of waiting to set your figures. There is no defensible universal site-purchase or per diem limit.


Test the draft against a real urgent purchase. If the approved route would have taken longer than the repair, shorten it. When a deadline forces a breach, let the responsible manager approve by phone or message and require a written record by the next working day. Someone else should review the exception afterwards.


Mark Smith, senior manager in Grant Thornton’s Business Risk Services team, advises auditors to “search expense claims at or just under approval cut-off levels” in his[ACCA guidance on expense controls](https://www.accaglobal.com/gb/en/member/sectors/internal-audit/our-publications/data-analytics-for-internal-auditors.html) . Repeated purchases just below a cap merit a closer look: the limit may be wrong, or orders may be split.


The policy should also say when the company provides a card, advance, or direct booking so a worker does not have to fund a large purchase personally. The[UAE Labour Law](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1541/download) bars charging workers recruitment and employment costs; it does not prescribe a general site-expense reimbursement rate. Set your arrangement clearly in the policy and relevant employment terms.


## Collect evidence and protect VAT recovery


An expense claim policy template should ask for the purchaser, supplier, date, item, amount, business reason, project code, approver, and proof of payment. If you intend to recover input VAT, finance must also check that the purchase qualifies and obtain a valid tax invoice. The[FTA’s input VAT guidance](https://tax.gov.ae/en/faq.aspx?keyword=Under+which+conditions+will+businesses+be+allowed+to+claim+VAT+incurred+on+expenses%3F) calls for documentation showing VAT paid. A card slip shows payment, not necessarily the details of a tax invoice.


Ask small suppliers near the site for the invoice before leaving. The[FTA’s tax-invoice guidance](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/06-Tax-Invoices.pdf) says a simplified tax invoice may be issued where a VAT-registered recipient’s supply is AED 10,000 or less, or the recipient is not VAT registered. A qualifying simplified invoice can omit some buyer details required on a full invoice, but it must still carry the prescribed tax details. Do not treat every till or card slip as sufficient.


If a receipt is missing, obtain a signed explanation, payment proof, supplier details, and manager approval; ask the supplier for a replacement invoice. Finance decides whether VAT can be claimed. An expense reimbursement policy template should separately state when a complete claim is paid and who handles a disputed claim.


Keep evidence with the transaction. The[FTA’s record-keeping guidance](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/2022/Get%20to%20know%20your%20Tax%20Obligations.pdf) states a general five-year VAT minimum and a 15-year period for records relating to real estate. Corporate tax records can require seven years, so apply the longest relevant period to a shared record.


## Make the policy usable on site


Put the short version where people buy: on their phones, in the site induction pack, or in the purchasing channel. Show the cap, the person to call, and the details to capture. Keep the full policy for exceptions and accounting treatment.


Build approved limits into cards where possible. Alaan[corporate cards](https://www.alaan.com/products/corporate-cards) can be assigned to staff with limits and allowed spending categories, as shown in an internal onboarding call. A separate Alaan support call showed team-level receipt and expense-submission settings. These are observations from calls, not published customer results; check the controls available on your account before describing a particular configuration.


That support call also showed what happens when a rule is unclear to the people using it: missing expense details had frozen a card and delayed an urgent payment. Review missing invoices, wrong project codes, purchases above the cap, and repeat emergency reasons each month. If the same exception keeps returning, fix the rule. Use the[expense policy builder](https://www.alaan.com/expense-policy-builder) to document the agreed wording and the guide to[turning policy rules into habits](https://www.alaan.com/blog/business-expense-policy-reinforcement) to help roll it out.


## FAQs


### How do I write an expense policy for a construction company?


Start with who can buy on site, the amount, the approver, and the evidence required. Add the project-code rule and test the draft against recent urgent purchases.


### What should I include for site-based staff?


Cover urgent materials, away-from-base accommodation and meals, tools, subcontractor purchases, fuel and mileage, and project coding. Give each situation a limit, approver, and evidence rule.


### What limits are reasonable?


Use your recent purchase and travel costs, then set caps by role and site. Decide the amount at which staff must call first and review exceptions after rollout.


### What if a receipt is missing?


Ask for payment proof, supplier details, and a signed explanation, then seek a replacement tax invoice. A manager can approve the business expense; finance must separately decide whether there is enough evidence to recover VAT.
